definition: A family of fine-tuning techniques that adapt a pretrained model by updating only a small subset or a small additional set of parameters, rather than the full model.
details: PEFT methods (including LoRA, adapters, and prefix tuning) reduce the compute, memory, and storage costs of customizing large models for new tasks or domains.

explainer.lead: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning is a family of techniques that adapt a pretrained model by updating only a small subset or small additional set of parameters. It matters because it cuts the compute, memory, and storage cost of customizing large models.

tiers.eli5: Instead of rewriting a whole textbook to add a new chapter, you stick in a few sticky notes that adjust the meaning.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers apply methods like LoRA, adapters, and prefix tuning to specialize large models for new tasks or domains without touching all weights. A pitfall is that only a small fraction of parameters is changed, so the adapter's capacity must be matched to how far the new task departs from the base model.
tiers.paperLevel: PEFT adapts a pretrained model by updating only a small subset or a small additional set of parameters rather than the full model; methods include LoRA, adapters, and prefix tuning, reducing compute, memory, and storage costs of customization.

explainer.example: Fine-tuning a large language model for a support-desk domain by training a LoRA adapter leaves the base weights frozen and stores only the small adapter.
